events.title: Napoleon Crowns Himself Emperor
events.description: In a lavish ceremony at Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris, Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French. He took the crown from the pope's hands and placed it on his own head.
events.significance: The coronation sealed Napoleon's transformation from revolutionary general to hereditary monarch and set the stage for a decade of European war.

events.title: Battle of Austerlitz
events.description: Exactly one year after his coronation, Napoleon's French army defeated a larger Russian and Austrian force in Moravia. Many consider it his greatest tactical victory.
events.significance: The win broke up the Third Coalition against France and led to the end of the Holy Roman Empire. It made Napoleon the dominant power in continental Europe.

events.title: The Monroe Doctrine Is Announced
events.description: In his annual message to Congress, President James Monroe warned European powers against any new colonization or interference in the Americas. In return, he pledged that the United States would stay out of European conflicts.
events.significance: The doctrine became a cornerstone of U.S. foreign policy for the next two centuries.

events.title: John Brown Is Hanged
events.description: Abolitionist John Brown was hanged in Virginia for his raid on the federal arsenal at Harpers Ferry, which he had led in October of that year.
events.significance: Brown's execution deepened the divide between North and South and made him a martyr to many abolitionists. It helped push the nation toward the Civil War.

events.title: First Permanent Artificial Heart Implant
events.description: At the University of Utah, retired dentist Barney Clark became the first person to receive a permanent artificial heart.
events.significance: The operation was a landmark in cardiac surgery. It paved the way for later mechanical heart technologies.
